function: Excluded, function: the DNN identifies which radar-detected object is the communication user, given the optimal beam index; it outputs no beam, waveform, or resource (pp. 2-4).
notes: Reason function (Step 1, rule 5). p. 2: "we aim to determine the communication target within the radar measurement" (Sec. III); p. 4: the network "returns the likelihood of the candidate object being the communication target", and the object with maximum probability is returned. The learned output is the index of the radar object that is the user (target identification and association between radar and communication domains), not a beam, waveform, or resource, so it does not solve the ISAC problem of area 5 as defined; the paper does not use it to predict beams. It is closer to target or emitter identification, which Step 1 lists as excluded. Borderline, because the work is radar-aided communication (title: ISAC) with a MISO mmWave base station (p. 1) and real DeepSense 6G Scenario 35 data, accuracy 0.9343 (p. 5, Table I); the reviewer should confirm the call. Eligibility checks 1 to 4 do not apply: it is a research letter, it proposes a DNN, and the object matching is made on radar and beam data, not on a network-level decision. The file is the arXiv preprint v1 of Nov 2024 (arXiv:2411.06578v1); the DOI is not printed in the file, so the DOI-to-paper match could not be checked from the PDF.
